Independent analytic tangent Hessian, local pushforward normalization and endpoint calculations
correctness.rationale: The projected generator lengths are sqrt(1−n_i²), and planar zonotope perimeter is twice their sum by additivity of widths. Strict concavity on the squared-coordinate simplex gives the six axis minima and eight diagonal maxima. For fixed z=|n_3|, the folded azimuth is uniform on [0,π/2]. Squaring the sum of the two variable radicals gives 1+z²+2 sqrt(z²+(1−z²)² sin²(2β)/4), which is increasing on the half-interval. Solving the threshold yields the stated radicand, and the two azimuth pieces give angular measure arcsin(sqrt(R)), so integrating their conditional probability over uniform z gives the unconditional CDF. The level z=1 is null. Away from the axes the Lagrange multiplier equation forces equal nonzero absolute coordinates. At the twelve saddles the tangent Hessian is diag(−2√2,2(√2−1)), obtained by subtracting the normal multiplier from the ambient diagonal Hessian; at each maximum it is −sqrt(3/2) times the identity. After Morse rescaling a saddle gives quadratic form x²−y² with weight at zero (4π sqrt(2−√2))^(−1). In u=x+y,v=x−y the Jacobian 1/2 cancels the two signs in the logarithmic integral, giving log(1/|p−p_*|) with unit coefficient; a smooth weight minus its value at zero is O(|u|+|v|), whose pushforward is bounded locally. Summing over twelve saddles gives the stated coefficient on both sides. Compact regular preimages give a smooth density, and the isolated critical directions carry no mass. At an axis, tangent radius r gives P−4=2r+O(r²), so six disks of radius ε/2+O(ε²) give 3ε²/8. At a diagonal the quadratic deficit is (√6/4)r², so eight disks give 4 sqrt(2/3) ε+o(ε). The use of full-sphere 1/(4π) throughout avoids a sign-quotient factor error; rescaling lengths divides the density coefficient by side length.
residual_risks: Recorded numerical window estimates and hull checks corroborate but do not prove the asymptotics. Smooth density here refers to the canonical regular-value density away from the unique interior critical value.

value.rationale: The random orthogonal perimeter of a unit cube is a natural projection statistic with known moments but nontrivial distribution shape. An explicit unique interior logarithmic divergence and distinct sharp endpoint probability scales quantify phenomena moments or a smoothed histogram cannot resolve. The exact coefficients, together with a one-dimensional CDF, are useful calibration and numerical benchmarks for projection distributions; the value is not the already-known zonotope perimeter identity.
residual_risks: Only the exact solid cube under Haar orthographic viewing is analyzed. The review does not claim a joint area–perimeter law, general cuboid classification, or priority over uninspected cuboid material.
